note: Comes before the article: tout le jour = the whole day; tous les jours = every day.
ex: Tous les jours. — Every day.

note: bon = good (adj); bien = well (adv). Le bon numéro = the right number.
ex: C'est la bonne réponse. — That's the right answer.

note: un grand homme = a great man; un homme grand = a tall man.
ex: Il est très grand. — He is very tall.

note: Before the noun = only (le seul ami); after/with être = alone (un homme seul).
ex: Je suis seul. — I am alone.
Une autre fois. — Another time.

note: sûr de = sure of; un endroit sûr = a safe place. Don't confuse with sur (on).
ex: Tu es sûr ? — Are you sure?

note: bel before a vowel (m.): un bel homme. Il fait beau = the weather is nice.
ex: Il fait beau. — The weather is nice.

note: Before the noun = real, genuine: un vrai ami = a real friend.
ex: C'est vrai ? — Is that true?
Le premier jour. — The first day.

note: la semaine dernière = last week (the one before); la dernière semaine = the final week.
ex: L'année dernière. — Last year.

faux: also = tight (clothes); adv. juste = just, only
ex: C'est juste. — That's right / That's fair.

note: vieil before a vowel (m.): un vieil ami.
gros = bulky, fat, heavy; grand = tall, great.
plein de = lots of (colloq.).
ex: Il y a plein de gens. — There are lots of people.

note: fol before a vowel (m.), rare: un fol espoir.

ex: Le mauvais numéro. — The wrong number.

note: prêt à + infinitive = ready to. Don't confuse with près (near). Noun le prêt = loan.
ex: Je suis prêt. — I'm ready.

note: ma propre voiture = my own car; une voiture propre = a clean car.
ex: Ma propre chambre. — My own room.

note: un pauvre homme = a pitiable man; un homme pauvre = a poor (not rich) man.

ex: Une jolie maison. — A pretty house.

note: Lowercase as adjective/language; un Français = a Frenchman.
Before the noun = dear (cher ami); after = expensive (un livre cher).
ex: C'est trop cher. — It's too expensive.

note: le meilleur = the best. Adjective of bon; the adverb is mieux.
ex: Mon meilleur ami. — My best friend.

note: Free = at liberty/available, NOT free of charge (= gratuit).
ex: Tu es libre ce soir ? — Are you free tonight?
Je suis désolé. — I'm sorry.

note: J'ai froid = I'm cold (not je suis froid).
Before the noun = some (certains jours); after = sure (un fait certain).

ex: C'est pareil. — It's the same.
bleu clair — light blue

note: en bas = downstairs / below; noun le bas = bottom; stocking.
content de = pleased with.
en haut = upstairs / above. Aspirated h: le haut, no liaison.

faux: ≠ facile (glib) — just means easy, no negative tone
ex: C'est facile. — It's easy.
Tu es gentil. — You're kind.

note: Before the noun = nasty: un sale type = a nasty guy.
ex: Tes mains sont sales. — Your hands are dirty.

note: drôle de + noun = strange: une drôle d'idée = a strange idea.
Ce n'est pas grave = it doesn't matter / no problem.
ex: Ce n'est pas grave. — It's no big deal.

faux: before the noun = former, not ancient
note: mon ancien prof = my former teacher; un château ancien = an old castle.
ex: Mon ancien patron. — My former boss.

note: Plural before the noun = various: différentes personnes.
la semaine prochaine = next week; la prochaine fois = next time.
ex: À la prochaine ! — See you next time!
Laisse-moi tranquille. — Leave me alone.

note: J'ai chaud = I'm hot; il fait chaud = it's hot (weather).

ex: Le moindre bruit. — The slightest noise.

faux: colloq. can mean great; pas terrible = not great
ex: Le film n'est pas terrible. — The film isn't great.

note: neuf = brand-new; nouveau = new/another. Also the number neuf = nine.
amoureux de = in love with.
Noun les frais = costs, expenses.
le pire = the worst.

ex: Une robe courte. — A short dress.
C'est génial ! — That's great!

note: Pronounced "segond"; deuxième is the more general word.
Used with pas, jamais, plus, rien…; often dropped in speech.
ex: Je ne sais pas. — I don't know.

note: Noun le pas = step.
ex: Pas maintenant. — Not now.

faux: ne … plus = no longer, not more
ex: Je n'ai plus faim. — I'm not hungry anymore.

note: bien = well (adv) vs bon = good (adj). bien sûr = of course.
ex: Tu parles bien. — You speak well.
Non, merci. — No, thank you.

note: To answer yes to a negative question use si.
ex: Oui, bien sûr. — Yes, of course.

note: In speech often means here: je suis là. -là = that: ce jour-là = that day.
ex: Je suis là. — I'm here.

note: si grand = so tall; also conj. si = if.
ex: Tu ne viens pas ? — Si ! — Aren't you coming? — Yes!
Viens ici. — Come here.
Alors, on y va ? — So, shall we go?

note: aussi grand que = as tall as.
ex: Moi aussi. — Me too.

note: pas encore = not yet; encore un = another one.
ex: Encore un café ? — Another coffee?
Très bien. — Very good.
Je ne fume jamais. — I never smoke.

note: Adv. même = even; le même = the same; moi-même = myself.
ex: Même lui est venu. — Even he came.
Il est toujours là. — He's still here.

note: peu = little, not much; un peu = a little, some.
ex: Un peu de sucre. — A little sugar.
C'est trop cher. — It's too expensive.

note: Don't confuse with peut être (can be).
ex: Peut-être demain. — Maybe tomorrow.
Pourquoi pas ? — Why not?
Viens maintenant. — Come now.
Tu es déjà allé à Paris ? — Have you ever been to Paris?
C'est vraiment bien. — It's really good.
Moins cher. — Cheaper.
Comment ça va ? — How are you?
Merci beaucoup. — Thanks a lot.

note: Comparative of bien (adv); meilleur is the adjective (of bon).
ex: Ça va mieux. — I'm feeling better.
Viens vite ! — Come quickly!
J'en ai assez. — I've had enough.

note: tant de = so much/many; tant que = as long as; tant pis = too bad.
ex: Tant pis. — Too bad.

note: Noun le mal = pain, evil: avoir mal à = to have a pain in.
ex: Il chante mal. — He sings badly.
Enfin seuls ! — Alone at last!
C'est loin d'ici. — It's far from here.

note: tard = late (in the day); en retard = late (behind schedule).
ex: Il est tard. — It's late.
Seulement deux euros. — Only two euros.
C'est ainsi. — That's how it is.
C'est presque fini. — It's almost done.
Il y a longtemps. — A long time ago.
À demain ! — See you tomorrow!
Aujourd'hui, il pleut. — Today it's raining.
C'est combien ? — How much is it?

note: plutôt que = rather than; ≠ plus tôt (earlier).
ex: C'est plutôt bien. — It's rather good.

note: d'ailleurs = besides, moreover.
ex: Allons ailleurs. — Let's go somewhere else.
Et pourtant, c'est vrai. — And yet it's true.

note: autour de = around (prep.).
ex: Autour de la table. — Around the table.
Parfois, je lis. — Sometimes I read.
Surtout, ne dis rien. — Above all, say nothing.
Il vient souvent. — He comes often.

note: Noun un ensemble = a set; an outfit.
ex: On mange ensemble ? — Shall we eat together?

note: autant de = as much/many; autant que = as much as.
ex: Autant que toi. — As much as you.

note: Adj. fort = strong.
ex: Parle plus fort. — Speak louder.
Il habite là-bas. — He lives over there.
À bientôt ! — See you soon!
C'est tellement beau. — It's so beautiful.
D'abord, on mange. — First, we eat.
Je t'ai cherché partout. — I looked everywhere for you.
Hier soir. — Last night.
Et ensuite ? — And then?
Il fait froid dehors. — It's cold outside.
Je me lève tôt. — I get up early.
Je suis debout. — I'm standing / I'm up.
C'est exactement ça. — That's exactly it.
Parle doucement. — Speak softly.

note: Also adj. soudain = sudden.
ex: Soudain, il est parti. — Suddenly he left.

note: au-dessus de = above (prep.).
ex: Au-dessus de la porte. — Above the door.
C'est simplement faux. — It's simply wrong.

note: Often weaker than English: sûrement = most likely.
ex: Il viendra sûrement. — He'll probably come.

note: aussitôt que = as soon as.
ex: Il est parti aussitôt. — He left at once.
C'est complètement fou. — It's completely crazy.
Parlez lentement. — Speak slowly.

note: là-dessus = on that; au-dessus = above; sens dessus dessous = upside down.
ex: Mets-le dessus. — Put it on top.
Cependant, il a raison. — However, he's right.
C'est absolument vrai. — It's absolutely true.
C'est justement le problème. — That's precisely the problem.
